items.text: Daniel and Rachel suggested that Emily continue her journey by train. There was a station nearby, they explained, and a train to Toronto would leave at noon. But what about my car? Emily asked anxiously. Daniel promised to have it towed out of the ditch and kept in his garage until she returned. The couple then drove her to the station and waited with her until the train arrived. Waving to them through the frosty train window, Emily could hardly hold back her tears. That evening, she fell into her boyfriend’s arms in Toronto, just in time for Christmas.

items.text: Three days later, Emily returned to get her car. The sky was clear now, and the road that had trapped her lay quiet in the sunshine. Parked outside the couple’s garage was her car, cleaned of snow and ready to go. Emily handed them a box of homemade cookies and a card that read, Thank you for saving my holiday. We just did what anyone would do, Rachel said, giving her a warm hug. Driving away, Emily realized that the storm had nearly ruined her Christmas, but two strangers had made it the warmest of her life.
